nodes.name: NiTe nanoarrays growth
nodes.procedure: NiTe nanoarrays grown on NF surface forming vertical cross-column nanoarrays with length of about 1 μm (details see Supplementary Material)
nodes.source_text: From the SEM images of NiTe (Fig. 1b and S1a), vertical cross-column nanoarrays, with the length of about 1μm (Fig. S2a), can be observed, suggesting that the NiTe arrays have successfully grown on the NF surface evenly.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of FeOOH
nodes.procedure: FeOOH electrodeposited on NiTe nanoarrays forming core-shell structured NiTe@FeOOH catalyst (details see Supplementary Material)
nodes.source_text: During the preparation process, the core-shell-structured catalyst NiTe@FeOOH was fabricated by electrodepositing FeOOH on the NiTe nanoarrays.

Fig. 3a illustrated the LSV curves of obtained catalysts in 1.0 M KOH... NiTe@FeOOH catalyst reveals the lowest overpotentials of 264 and 304 mV to attain 100 and 500 mA cm−2... Tafel slope of 52 mV dec−1... ECSA values... 135.0... Rct value of about 3.57... after 100 h of continuous operation at 100 mA cm−2, no obvious potential increasement was observed (Fig. 3e)

Fig. 3f... NiTe@FeOOH exhibited the highest HER performance, with the lowest overpotentials of 279 and 359 mV at 100 mA cm−2 and 500 mA cm−2... Tafel slope of 99 mV dec−1... After 100 h continuous measurements at 100 mA cm−2, no obvious performance degradation was seen (Fig. 3h)

Fig. 4a... OER performance of NiTe@FeOOH... in alkaline seawater... overpotentials as low as 280 and 328 mV to achieved 100 and 500 mA cm−2... U-t curve... After 100 h continuous measurements at 100 mA cm−2, no obvious performance degradations were seen (Fig. 4d)

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of NiTe show vertical cross-column nanoarrays with length of about 1 μm; NiTe@FeOOH shows little morphological change with thin deposited layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the SEM images of NiTe (Fig. 1b and S1a), vertical cross-column nanoarrays, with the length of about 1μm (Fig. S2a), can be observed... After the electrochemical deposition procedure, little changes in the morphology were seen, suggesting that the deposited layer on the NiTe was thin (Fig. 1c and S1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms column-like nanostructures of NiTe and NiTe@FeOOH with thin FeOOH layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images of NiTe (Fig. 1d) and NiTe@FeOOH (Fig. 1e) further confirmed the column-like nanostructures of NiTe and NiTe@FeOOH, as well as the thin layer of FeOOH in NiTe@FeOOH (Fig. S2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringe spacing of 0.30 nm corresponding to (101) plane of NiTe in both samples; absence of FeOOH lattice fringes indicates amorphous FeOOH in NiTe@FeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images of NiTe and NiTe@FeOOH in Fig. 1f and g revealed the lattice fringe spacing of 0.30nm, which is corresponding to the (101) plane of NiTe... The absence of FeOOH related lattice in the HRTEM image of NiTe@FeOOH suggests that the FeOOH deposited on the surface is amorphous.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS elemental mapping confirms core-shell structure of NiTe@FeOOH with Ni and Te signals mainly in the center and Fe and O signals mainly on the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To evaluate the distributions of various elements in NiTe@FeOOH, Scanning TEM and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDX) mapping measurements were conducted. As illustrated in Fig. 1h and i and S4, obvious Fe, O, Ni and Te signals are observed in NiTe@FeOOH. Additionally, it can be further observed that Ni and Te mainly existed in the center of NiTe@FeOOH, while Fe and O majorly distributed on the surface, verifying that NiTe@FeOOH is core-shell structured.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiTe@FeOOH composition: Ni 2.80 at%, Te 1.35 at%, Fe 1.07 at%, O 19.18 at%. O 1s peaks at 530.61, 531.81, 533.31 eV (Fe-O-H, Fe-O-Fe, H2O); Fe 2p peaks at 732.04, 725.24, 716.14, 711.64 eV (Fe3+); Ni 2p and Te 3d shift positively by 0.21 eV and 0.33 eV vs NiTe, indicating electron transfer interactions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 2a and b, NiTe@FeOOH was composed by Ni, Te, Fe and O, with atomic contents of 2.80, 1.35, 1.07 and 19.18 at%, respectively... the Ni 2p and Te 3d shifted positively by 0.21 and 0.33eV respectively after FeOOH was deposited, suggesting their lower electron density than sole NiTe, and verifying that there exist interactions between NiTe and deposited FeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiTe: -3.23 mV; FeOOH: 14.7 mV; NiTe@FeOOH: -1.11 mV, indicating enhanced Cl- repelling ability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiTe has the most negative Zeta potential of -3.23mV, while FeOOH has the most positive value of 14.7mV. Obviously, NiTe@FeOOH had more negative Zeta potential (-1.11mV) than sole NiTe (-3.23mV), but lower than that of FeOOH (14.7mV).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of NiTe@FeOOH show absence of FeOOH-related diffraction peaks, confirming amorphous FeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absence of FeOOH related lattice in the HRTEM image of NiTe@FeOOH suggests that the FeOOH deposited on the surface is amorphous, which can be also confirmed by the absence of FeOOH related diffraction peaks in its XRD patterns (Fig. S3).
